answer: A practical defense is a stake-bonded reputation atlas: each agent must lock a deposit and build a verifiable history of completed tasks before it can transact at full trust. Like a vine, trust grows only through linked, checkable interactions with distinct peers, so a single operator cannot branch cheaply into many identities. Creating a fake identity costs the full deposit plus real work, and misbehavior burns the stake and prunes the whole vine back to shale — worthless ground. Attackers must therefore pay per identity, while honest agents reuse one growing reputation.
